column7: mintSession (internal/core/auth.go) discarded a RETURNED error from its best-effort EnforceSessionLimit call but had no panic protection, so a panic there propagated past the already-committed Session row and out through the transport's panic-recovery wrapper as a 500 -- misreporting an already-successful login, and for the POST /auth/mfa/verify caller also an already-CONSUMED TOTP step, as a failure. FuzzStorageFaultOperations found it on #2392 (oracle (a), differing tables [LoginAttempt Session MFASecret]). Fixed in #2416: the call runs under besteffort.Run, which recovers a panic the same way the returned error was already absorbed. Every session-minting path funnels through mintSession (Login, setup-token consume x2, SSO complete, VerifyMFALogin), confirmed as the single EnforceSessionLimit call site in internal/core, so this closure covers the family and not just the MFA-verify instance. Two independent non-vacuity checks, both run by FIX-2 against the pre-#2416 shape (besteffort.Run replaced by a bare discarded call): the named proving test goes red, and the committed fuzz seed testdata/fuzz/FuzzStorageFaultOperations/mfa-verify-enforcesessionlimit-panic-2416 reproduces the issue's exact signature ("ORACLE (a) VIOLATION ... Differing tables: [LoginAttempt Session MFASecret]"). That seed is index-addressed, so FIX-2 also registered it in seed_v2_test.go's seedIntent table, without which it could silently re-point to a different op/method on any storage-layer PR and keep passing under this claim's name.
